note: `exports` measured GAP -> implemented. Elixir has no export-list statement (the erlang lane's `-export([f/a])` has no counterpart), so the public callable surface is read off the declarations: def/defmacro/defguard/defdelegate/defexception publish, defp/defmacrop/defguardp do not. This is a DIFFERENT statement from `contains` (is a member) — it is the set another module can call as `Mod.f(...)`, which is what bb_migrate's cross-language mapping and the go/java/kotlin exports edges carry, and the only channel that reaches the store (parallel-indexer writes imports[] to brain_import and declares no brain_export table, so the 1,201 ExportInfo this analyzer already published were never persisted). Measured on 559 corpus files: 4,031 edges in 411 files, both endpoints resolving 4031/4031. Falsifier: mutant elixir/exports-private-published, elixir/exports-owner-any-kind, elixir/exports-line-wrong. Three rules are pinned by their MUTANT rather than by an expected edge, because each forbids an edge that must never exist: a member with no module owner (the .exs script shape) publishes no export surface, a non-callable member (struct field, type alias) is not an export, and a private definition is not published whatever its name says.
